title: Feature-Flag Substrate Canonical Spec
purpose: Operationalizes ADR-0159. Declares OpenFeature compliance, evaluation context shape, Cedar-predicate-based targeting, lifecycle gating, audit-chain emission policy, per-cell replication semantics.

evaluation_context_shape.persona_tier: string (required) — one of {personal, team, business, enterprise, sovereign}
evaluation_context_shape.user_id_hash: string (optional) — SHA-256 over user_id; raw user_id forbidden

lifecycle._ci_lane_is_an_unimplemented_claim: NO CI lane, workflow or gate named `feature-flag-lifecycle` exists anywhere in the tree — measured by whole-tree `git grep feature-flag-lifecycle` at merge-base 8857944612 and at this head, which return the same six hits and no implementation. The value below is doubly misleading: it names a lane that does not exist, AND it names an `oya gate validate` CLI invocation, which under the repo cli_surface_policy is local bridge feedback and NEVER merge authority, so even a working CLI would not be the enforcement this reads as. See the matching note in flags/release/runtime-safety-policy.json for why the sibling key there cannot simply be deleted (it is enum-pinned by contract-slice-conformance in two places).
violations: code references flag whose definition no longer exists

audit_chain_emission.on_evaluation: only if flag tagged audit_required: true (used for kill-switches + compliance-gated features)

cedar_predicate_evaluator.rationale: one Cedar evaluator path; multiple consumers (auth + feature-flag)

anti_patterns_forbidden: ENV-var feature flags in workload µservices
ChangeSet acceptance_status used as runtime gate
Commercial SaaS feature-flag dependency in sovereign packs (per ADR-0049 + ADR-0164)
Cedar policy used as substitute for feature flag (different SLAs, different audit requirements)
